_comment: Lockfile fixture for the dependencies-vulnerable calibration case. Deliberately pins a
package version with a known advisory so `npm audit` returns a real finding, giving
DependenciesAgent a positive case it previously lacked (both its cases were expectEmpty, so a
WHY this is named vulnerable-lockfile.json and not package-lock.json: GitHub's Dependabot
security alerts key on the package-lock.json FILENAME and scan every match in the repo,
regardless of .github/dependabot.yml (which only configures github-actions updates here).
Committing this as a real lockfile would raise permanent alerts on a repo that deliberately
maintains `npm audit` 0, trading a live security signal for a test fixture. calibrate.ts
copies this into a temp directory as package-lock.json at run time instead, which keeps the
fixture deterministic and committed without touching the repo's own audit surface.
No `npm install` is required: npm audit resolves advisories from the lockfile alone, verified
against this exact content (exit 1, vulnerabilities.lodash, 1 critical).
npm ignores unknown top-level keys, so this _comment block does not affect the audit.
name: acr-calibration-vulnerable-fixture
